title: Cohen--Macaulay open restriction meeting every orbit
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention], and let $V,R$ be $S$-schemes. An equivalence relation $(s,t):R\to V\times_SV$ [def-pc-fibre-product] means that for every $S$-scheme $T$ the map on sections is injective and identifies $R(T)$ with an equivalence relation on $V(T)$. A morphism $f:X\to Y$ is called Cohen--Macaulay here if it is flat [def-weil-flat-morphism] and every local ring of every scheme-theoretic fibre [def-pc-scheme-fibre] is Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], with depth [def-weil-pbc-depth] equal to Krull dimension [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring]. Assume $s,t$ are flat and locally of finite presentation [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. There is an open subscheme $W\subseteq V$ [def-weil-open-immersion] such that the restricted relation $R_W=W\times_{V,t}R\times_{s,V}W$ has Cohen--Macaulay, locally finitely presented projections to $W$, and the map $h_W=s\circ\operatorname{pr}_R:W\times_{V,t}R\to V$ is surjective, flat and locally of finite presentation.

proof.text: For any flat locally finitely presented $f:X\to Y$, let $C_f$ be the set of points where the fibre local ring has depth equal to dimension. Its fibres are locally Noetherian by [lem-sbc-restricted-fibre-locally-noetherian], taking the open to be all of $Y$. Thus this is precisely its Cohen--Macaulay locus as defined in the statement, and it is open by [lem-sbc-fibre-cohen-macaulay-locus-open].

These opens meet the compatibility hypotheses of [lem-sfb-relation-open-locus-descent]. Indeed for a cartesian square with flat locally finitely presented vertical maps $f,f'$, [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-of-base-change] identifies the fibre at $y'$ with $X_y\times_{\kappa(y)}\kappa(y')$. The fibre $X_y$ is locally of finite type over $\kappa(y)$: on an affine presentation $B=A[x_1,\ldots,x_n]/(q_1,\ldots,q_m)$ its fibre algebra is $\kappa(y)[x_1,\ldots,x_n]/(\bar q_1,\ldots,\bar q_m)$. The first assertion of [lem-pur-cohen-macaulay-field-extension] therefore gives $x'\in C_{f'}$ if and only if $\operatorname{pr}_X(x')\in C_f$. It requires no Noetherian hypothesis on $Y$ or $Y'$. Isomorphisms of morphisms induce isomorphisms of fibre local rings; transporting regular sequences and prime chains preserves depth and dimension. Hence $C_f$ is also invariant under these isomorphisms.

Reflexivity evaluated at $T=V$ gives the unique $e:V\to R$ over $(\mathrm{id},\mathrm{id})$. Symmetry evaluated at $T=R$ gives $i:R\to R$ over $(t,s)$; injectivity on sections gives $i^2=\mathrm{id}$. Apply [lem-sfb-relation-open-locus-descent] to the assignment $D_f=C_f$. We obtain the open $W=e^{-1}(C_s)$ with $t^{-1}(W)=C_s$. Since $s i=t$, the fibre local rings for $t$ at $r$ and for $s$ at $i(r)$ are isomorphic. Thus $C_t=i^{-1}(C_s)=s^{-1}(W)$.

source.place: Tag 0460, lemma-make-CM, proof of (1),(2), using Tag 04LH

proof.text: The source of $h_W$ is the open $t^{-1}(W)$ of $R$ by the defining universal property of the fibre product. By [lem-trf-flat-lfp-cm-locus-fibre-dense], $C_s\cap R_v$ is dense in each fibre $R_v$ of $s$. Every such fibre is nonempty: $e(v)$ is a point over $v$. Applying density to the nonempty open subset $R_v$ itself gives a point in $C_s\cap R_v=t^{-1}(W)\cap R_v$. Therefore $h_W$ is surjective. This also covers $V=\varnothing$, when surjectivity is vacuous.

source.place: Tag 0460, lemma-make-CM, proof of (3),(4); more-morphisms.tex, Tag 045U (3)

proof.text: An open inclusion is etale by [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-etale]. Consequently precomposing either $s$ or $t$ with any source-open inclusion preserves flatness and local finite presentation by clause (i) of [lem-sfb-scheme-etale-source-target-properties]. In particular $h_W=s|_{t^{-1}(W)}$ is flat and locally of finite presentation. The open $R_W=t^{-1}(W)\cap s^{-1}(W)$ is the indicated iterated fibre product, by its universal property. Its two projections factor uniquely through $W$.

source.place: Tag 0460, lemma-make-CM (5); groupoids.tex, restriction construction; restrictions to source opens

proof.text: Write $j:W\hookrightarrow V$ and $k:R_W\hookrightarrow R$. For each projection $p:R_W\to W$, the square $j p=s k$ or $j p=t k$ has etale horizontal maps $k,j$. The commutative-square clause of [lem-sfb-scheme-etale-source-target-properties] gives flatness and local finite presentation of $p$. At a point of $R_W$, its fibre over $w\in W$ is the open restriction of the corresponding fibre of $s$ or $t$ over $j(w)$. Indeed [def-weil-open-immersion] identifies $\mathcal O_{W,w}$ with $\mathcal O_{V,j(w)}$, hence their residue fields, and the fibre-product universal property identifies this fibre with the inverse image of $R_W$ in the original fibre. Its local ring is therefore the same fibre local ring. Since $R_W\subset C_s\cap C_t$, that ring is Noetherian and has depth equal to dimension. Both projections are Cohen--Macaulay.

lean.statement: theorem exists_flat_relation_cm_open {S : Scheme.{u}} {V R : Over S} (s t : R ⟶ V) (hinj : ∀ T : Over S, Function.Injective (fun r : T ⟶ R ↦ (r ≫ s, r ≫ t))) (hrel : ∀ T : Over S, Equivalence (fun a b : T ⟶ V ↦ ∃ r : T ⟶ R, r ≫ s = a ∧ r ≫ t = b)) [Flat s.left] [Flat t.left] [LocallyOfFinitePresentation s.left] [LocallyOfFinitePresentation t.left] : ∃ W : V.left.Opens, (∀ p : pullback (pullback.snd W.ι t.left ≫ s.left) W.ι ⟶ W.toScheme, (p = pullback.fst (pullback.snd W.ι t.left ≫ s.left) W.ι ≫ pullback.fst W.ι t.left ∨ p = pullback.snd (pullback.snd W.ι t.left ≫ s.left) W.ι) → Flat p ∧ LocallyOfFinitePresentation p ∧ ∀ (w : W.toScheme) (x : p.fiber w), IsNoetherianRing ((p.fiber w).presheaf.stalk x) ∧ (IsLocalRing.depth (R := (p.fiber w).presheaf.stalk x) ((p.fiber w).presheaf.stalk x) : WithBot ℕ∞) = ringKrullDim ((p.fiber w).presheaf.stalk x)) ∧ Surjective (pullback.snd W.ι t.left ≫ s.left) ∧ Flat (pullback.snd W.ι t.left ≫ s.left) ∧ LocallyOfFinitePresentation (pullback.snd W.ι t.left ≫ s.left)
